title: Rotate three elements
starter:
%b  = buffer 3 dtype=i32 slot=0 data=[1 2 3]
%e0 = shrink %b 0 shape=[]
%e1 = shrink %b 1 shape=[]
%y  = load %e1
%s0 = store %e0 %y          # b[0] = b[1]
%b1 = after %b %s0
%f1 = shrink %b1 1 shape=[]
%f2 = shrink %b1 2 shape=[]
%z  = load %f2
%s1 = store %f1 %z          # b[1] = b[2]
%b2 = after %b1 %s1
%g0 = shrink %b2 0 shape=[]
%x  = load %g0              # meant to be the old b[0]
%g2 = shrink %b2 2 shape=[]
%s2 = store %g2 %x          # b[2] = old b[0]
%b3 = after %b2 %s2

hints: Write down which version each load reads, and what that version holds at that point. Which load sees a value that has already been overwritten?
The last store needs the original `b[0]`. Version `%b2` no longer has it; version `%b` does.
Load the old `b[0]` from version `%b` (the view `%e0` already exists). Rule 3 schedules that load before the store that overwrites `b[0]`, so it sees the original value.

answer.code:
%b  = buffer 3 dtype=i32 slot=0 data=[1 2 3]
%e0 = shrink %b 0 shape=[]
%e1 = shrink %b 1 shape=[]
%y  = load %e1
%s0 = store %e0 %y          # b[0] = b[1]
%b1 = after %b %s0
%f1 = shrink %b1 1 shape=[]
%f2 = shrink %b1 2 shape=[]
%z  = load %f2
%s1 = store %f1 %z          # b[1] = b[2]
%b2 = after %b1 %s1
%x  = load %e0              # the old b[0]: read version %b, before %s0 overwrites it
%g2 = shrink %b2 2 shape=[]
%s2 = store %g2 %x          # b[2] = old b[0]
%b3 = after %b2 %s2
answer.explain: Each load reads the version it names, so `load %e0` sees the original `b[0]` even though the first store overwrites that element. Rule 3 makes this possible: a load of version `%b` is scheduled before the store that creates `%b1`. The starter read `b[0]` from `%b2`, after it had already become the old `b[1]`.
